title: Working at Redwood: Roles, Career Ladders, Benefits, Hiring & Onboarding, and Internal Tools
author: Aisha Patel
content:
Overview

This document is the canonical company handbook entry for working at Redwood. It consolidates the most-requested topics for new and current employees: an overview of roles and career ladders, our approach to promotions and calibration, benefits and perks, the hiring and onboarding flows, a practical new-hire checklist, first-90-day expectations, and a quick reference to internal tools and support contacts.

Who this is for

- New hires across engineering, product, research, go-to-market, and core functions.
- Managers responsible for hiring, onboarding, and career development.
- Any employee looking for benefits, payroll, or tool access guidance.

Key sections (quick links)

1. Roles & career ladders
2. Promotions & calibration
3. Benefits & perks
4. Hiring & onboarding overview
5. New-hire checklist & first 90 days
6. Internal tools guide

1) Roles & career ladders

Short intro: Redwood’s career ladders describe expectations at each level for core functions so managers and individual contributors have transparent criteria for hiring, performance reviews, and promotions. Ladders are outcome-oriented and focus on scope, impact, craft, and leadership.

Engineering (example ladder summary)

| Level | Title example | Core expectations | Typical timeline |
|-------|---------------|-------------------|------------------|
| IC1   | Software Engineer I | Owns small features, writes maintainable code, participates in on-call; learns internal runtime architecture | 12-18 months |
| IC2   | Software Engineer II | Delivers end-to-end features, mentors junior engineers, contributes to design reviews | 18-36 months |
| IC3   | Senior Software Engineer | Leads cross-team projects, influences architecture, measurable product impact (latency/cost/quality) | 24-48 months |
| IC4   | Staff Engineer | Technical strategy for a domain, drives performance and reliability initiatives | Variable |
| IC5+  | Principal / Distinguished | Company-wide technical leadership, sets long-term platform roadmap | Variable |

Product & Design (summary)

- Product PM levels emphasize discovery, roadmap prioritization, metrics-driven delivery, and cross-functional leadership.
- Design levels emphasize craft, user research, and design systems contributions.

Applied ML / Research (summary)

- Focus areas: model quality, evals, model-serving tradeoffs, reproducible experiments, and model onboarding for inference.

Management track

- Engineering managers are evaluated on team health, delivery, hiring effectiveness, and coaching. People-ops partners to provide manager training and calibration materials.

Career conversations and resources

- Schedule a career conversation at least once per cycle with your manager.
- Handbook reference pages: performance-review-process, calibration-guidelines, leveling-examples (see Related Pages).

2) Promotions & calibration

Principles

- Promotions are based on demonstrated impact against ladder criteria, not tenure.
- Calibration panels ensure consistent expectations across teams.
- Managers must provide evidence (projects, PRs, metrics, demo artifacts) when nominating someone for promotion.

Promotion process (high level)

1. Manager nominates candidate with written justification and evidence.
2. Candidate dossier added to calibration queue.
3. Panel reviews dossier (manager peers + cross-functional reps + people-ops).
4. Outcome communicated; retro feedback provided.

Timing and cycles

- Promotions typically align with performance review cycles (mid-year and year-end) but can be processed ad-hoc for exceptional cases.

3) Benefits & perks

Healthcare and financial benefits

- Medical, dental, and vision plans with multiple tier options (employee-only through family). Employer covers a defined percentage of premiums; refer to the benefits enrollment guide for current rates.
- 401(k) with company match (up to 4% after eligibility period).
- Competitive equity grants for all full-time employees; refresh guidelines are in compensation docs.

Paid time off and leave

- Generous PTO policy plus 10 company-wide holidays.
- Parental leave: 16 weeks fully paid primary caregiver leave; 8 weeks for secondary caregivers; flexible phased return options.
- Bereavement leave and short-term disability per policy.

Perks and wellbeing

- Work-from-home stipend (USD 250 one-time and USD 50/month for remote office supplies).
- Professional development stipend (USD 2,000/year) and learning reimbursement.
- Mental health support via our EAP, plus 6 confidential sessions paid by Redwood.
- Annual company offsite travel supported for in-office teams.

Expense & travel policy highlights

- Use the Expense app for all reimbursements; policies on allowable expenses and approval flows are in the finance playbook.

4) Hiring & onboarding overview

Recruiting principles

- Hiring is collaborative: use structured interviews and shared rubrics.
- Commit to inclusive hiring practices: diverse slates, interviewer training, and score-based decisions.

Interview flow (engineering example)

1. Hire request and approvals (hiring manager + recruiting + finance).
2. Sourcing and screen (30-45 minute phone screen by recruiter + 1 technical screen).
3. On-site loop (remote): 4-5 interviews covering coding/design, systems, product sense, and culture.
4. Debrief and decision; recruiter prepares offer.

Offer & background checks

- Offers are issued by Recruiting in coordination with People Ops and Finance. Salary bands, equity guidelines, and sign-off steps are in the compensation playbook.
- Background checks and employment eligibility checks are required prior to start date.

Onboarding: owner and timeline

- People Ops owns the onboarding program; hiring manager owns role-specific ramp.
- Standard timeline:
  1) Pre-start (2 weeks): offer acceptance, paperwork, IT provisioning, welcome packet.
  2) Day 0-1: orientation, benefits enrollment, security training, Slack/Okta access.
  3) Week 1: team orientation, dev environment setup, first task assigned.
  4) Month 1: deliver a small project, meet cross-functional partners.
  5) Month 3: 90-day check-in, confirm goals and expectations.

5) New-hire checklist & first 90 days

New-hire checklist (must complete within first week)

- [ ] HR paperwork and benefits enrollment
- [ ] Complete security and compliance training
- [ ] Access to Slack, Okta, email, Confluence, Jira, and Redwood Console
- [ ] Local dev environment: clone repos, run local server, pass basic test suite
- [ ] Schedule 1:1s with manager and primary stakeholders

First 90 days: milestones for ICs

- 30 days: Understand product, team roadmap, and shipping process; complete small bug/feature.
- 60 days: Independently deliver a feature with tests and documentation; participate in on-call rotation if applicable.
- 90 days: Present a demo of your primary contribution; set growth plan with manager.

Manager checklist (first 90 days)

- Provide clear onboarding goals and a first-project plan.
- Schedule weekly 1:1s and provide timely feedback.
- Assign a peer buddy to support technical and cultural integration.

6) Internal tools guide (quick reference)

- Slack: Primary communication. Use #announcements for company-wide posts; respect channel scope.
- Okta: Single sign-on for all apps. Submit access requests via the IT portal for services requiring elevation.
- Confluence: Company documentation system. This handbook is the reference point for people policies. Use templates for docs and link related pages.
- Jira: Ticketing for engineering and product work. Follow our issue-type taxonomy: Bug, Story, Task, Chore.
- Redwood Console: Internal product observability and billing for sandbox environments. Access is role-based; request access via the infra ticket queue.
- Dev environments: Docker-based local dev with a standard repo template. See eng-developer-experience/dev-setup for CLI commands and sample docker-compose.

Support & escalation paths

- HR/People Ops: people-ops@example.redwood.com (for benefits, leave, and policy questions).
- IT & Access: it-support@example.redwood.com (Okta, hardware requests).
- Security incidents: security@example.redwood.com or PagerDuty for incidents (see incident-response-security).

FAQs (short)

Q: How do I request a promotion?
A: Talk to your manager to build a promotion dossier. Manager submits to calibration per the Promotions process above.

Q: Where do I find my equity and compensation details?
A: Compensation and equity specifics are on the compensation playbook (People Ops restricted view). Contact total-rewards@redwood.com for questions.

Q: Who do I contact if my laptop isn't working on Day 1?
A: Open an IT ticket and contact your manager and assigned buddy; emergency hardware requests use the IT Slack channel.
